$comment: #1379 — recorded HIGH/CRITICAL findings in the container images that have NO fix yet.
Read by scripts/lib/image-scan-gate.mjs (ci.yml `api`, build-images.yml). Policy, in short:
a fixable HIGH/CRITICAL always fails unless its entry sets allowFixed; an unfixed CRITICAL
fails unless recorded here; an unfixed HIGH not recorded here is a warning; and an entry
whose `expires` date has passed FAILS the gate while its finding is still present.
`expires` is a REVIEW date: on it, check whether the distro has shipped a fix. If it has,
rebuild (the images apply distro updates at build time) and MOVE the entry to `expired`;
if not, re-date it deliberately. Never re-date only to clear a red build.
An entry never simply disappears: any finding matching an id in `expired` FAILS, and on a
pull request a waiver deleted from `waivers` (and not moved to `expired`) FAILS while its
finding is present. So removing the record is never a way to turn a red build green.
Fields: id (CVE/GHSA), expires (a real YYYY-MM-DD date), reason, images (optional list of
image labels: server, ui, embeddings-svc, sql-lineage; absent = all), allowFixed (optional,
for a fix that exists but cannot be installed yet — keep that window short).
`expired` entries: id, retired (YYYY-MM-DD), reason, images (optional).
`allowFixed` entries must also list `packages` (exact name@installed copies), so they cannot
hide a different copy of the same package that CAN take the fix (#1489). An npm finding that
the OSV Dependency-audit gate already waives under a GHSA carries `mirrors` (that GHSA) and
`guards` (its reachability tests): it must match the sast.yml WAIVERS entry's expires and
packages exactly (scripts/lib/image-scan-waivers-mirror.test.mjs). Retire both together.
An empty `waivers` list is the goal.

libcurl3t64-gnutls 8.14.1-2+deb13u7, pulled in by git (#2395): no fix in Debian trixie on 2026-11-13 (no-dsa, minor).
